import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Convert the 'Dt_Customer' column to datetime format
data['Dt_Customer'] = pd.to_datetime(data['Dt_Customer'])

# Group by the 'Marital_Status' and 'Education' columns and calculate the average of 'Income'
grouped_data = data.groupby(['Marital_Status', 'Education']).agg({'Income': 'mean'})

# Pivot the data for easier plotting
pivoted_data = grouped_data.unstack('Education')

# Create a heatmap
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.heatmap(pivoted_data, annot=True, cmap='Blues', fmt='.2f')

# Add a title and labels
plt.title('Average Income by Marital Status and Education')
plt.xlabel('Marital Status')
plt.ylabel('Education')

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Convert the 'Dt_Customer' column to datetime format
data['Dt_Customer'] = pd.to_datetime(data['Dt_Customer'])

# Group by the 'Marital_Status' and 'Education' columns and calculate the average of 'Income'
grouped_data = data.groupby(['Marital_Status', 'Education']).agg({'Income': 'mean'})

# Pivot the data for easier plotting
pivoted_data = grouped_data.unstack('Education')

# Create a heatmap
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.heatmap(pivoted_data, annot=True, cmap='Blues', fmt='.2f')

# Add a title and labels
plt.title('Average Income by Marital Status and Education')
plt.xlabel('Marital Status')
plt.ylabel('Education')

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
